sentences.zh: 我想这算不上最显而易见的选角。

sentences.zh: 不管怎样，特洛伊是我们今天讨论的主题。

sentences.zh: 和我在一起的是布里克斯顿的阿喀琉斯，汤姆·赫兰德。

sentences.en: And after last week's discussion of 1981, this is a bit of an away fixture for me and a home match for Tom.
sentences.zh: 继上周讨论1981年之后，对我来说这算是一场客场比赛，而对汤姆来说是主场。

sentences.zh: 我们来到你的主战场了，对吧？

sentences.en: The fans are gathering in the stands.
sentences.zh: 球迷们正在看台上聚集。

sentences.en: So the peg for this is the all-conquering Leviathan that is Stephen Fry has a new book out on Troy, which tells you everything you need to know about the fascination with it.
sentences.zh: 所以这个话题的由头是，无所不能的巨头斯蒂芬·弗라이出了一本关于特洛伊的新书，这说明了人们对它有多着迷。

sentences.en: But a personal peg for me is that I'm currently reading my son.
sentences.zh: 但我个人的由头是我目前正在和我儿子一起读。

sentences.en: His bedtime reading is a children's version of the Iliad, which he is loving, actually.
sentences.zh: 他睡前读的是儿童版的《伊利亚特》，他其实非常喜欢。

sentences.en: And I would add that I'm actually right in the middle of writing a sequel to the Trojan War, which is a history for...
sentences.zh: 而且我要补充的是，我其实正在埋头写《特洛伊战争》的续集，那是一部关于……

sentences.en: Yeah, Troy 2.
sentences.zh: 对，特洛伊2。

sentences.en: History of ancient Greece for children in which the gods continue to play lead roles.
sentences.zh: 给儿童看的古希腊史，神明们在其中继续扮演主角。

sentences.en: So you still get Zeus and Athena and everything.
sentences.zh: 所以你还能看到宙斯、雅典娜以及各种神。

sentences.en: So coming to a bookshop next summer, folks.
sentences.zh: 所以各位，明年夏天将在书店与大家见面。

sentences.zh: 但在此之前，让我们先读几条关于之前节目的评论。

sentences.zh: 杰米·金斯顿在上周的节目后联系了我们。

sentences.zh: 在这期节目里，我不记得是哪一期了……

sentences.zh: 哦，当然是1981年这期。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 在这期节目中，我们了解到多米尼克讨厌婚礼和皇室婚礼。

sentences.zh: 尤其是皇室婚礼，对吧？

sentences.zh: 我讨厌婚礼。

sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.zh: 而且伊恩·博瑟姆其实是个维多利亚时代的人。

sentences.zh: 他是维多利亚时代的，还是说更偏向……

sentences.zh: 是的，大概吧。

sentences.zh: 然后当然了，他身上也非常具有20世纪80年代的色彩，这也是上周播客讨论的内容。

sentences.en: So Stuart Scott said, I'd take 1981 over 2020 at the drop of a hat.
sentences.zh: 所以斯图尔特·斯科特说，相比2020年，我毫不犹豫地选择1981年。

sentences.en: I guess probably quite a lot of people would agree with that, though perhaps not in Toxteth.
sentences.zh: 我想大概会有相当多的人同意这一点，尽管托克斯泰斯的人可能不会。

sentences.zh: 或者说我住的布里克斯顿也不会。

sentences.en: One of the principal characters of 1981 was, of course, Margaret Thatcher, who we described as highly divisive.
sentences.zh: 1981年的主要人物之一当然是玛格丽特·撒切尔，我们称她为极具分裂性的人物。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's kind of written into the...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这可以说是写进了……

sentences.en: That's the rule, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是规矩，对吧？

sentences.en: You can't mention Margaret Thatcher without saying highly divisive.
sentences.zh: 你提到玛格丽特·撒切尔就不能不说极具分裂性。

sentences.en: Controversial prime minister.
sentences.zh: 争议重重的首相。

sentences.en: And this prompted an interesting question from someone who calls himself or herself or itself wrecked on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 这引发了一个有趣的问题，提问者在推特上的名字叫wreck。

sentences.en: And he, she, or it asks, can you name the last undivisive prime minister?
sentences.zh: 他、她或它问，你能说出上一位不具分裂性的首相是谁吗？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, prime ministers are divisive by their own nature, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，首相天生就具有分裂性，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, because to govern is to choose and to choose between two different camps.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为治理就是抉择，就是在两个不同的阵营之间做出选择。

sentences.en: But I suppose some...
sentences.zh: 但我想有些……

sentences.en: So there are prime ministers who stock in trade is to be emollient, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 所以有些首相的看家本领就是表现得温和圆滑，对吧？

sentences.en: David Cameron, let's say.
sentences.zh: 比方说大卫·卡梅伦。

sentences.en: Tony Blair before Iraq.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克战争前的托尼·布莱尔。

sentences.en: Was Harold Wilson that divisive?
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·威尔逊那么具有分裂性吗？

sentences.en: Was Jim Callaghan?
sentences.zh: 吉姆·卡拉汉呢？

sentences.en: I'm not convinced they were, really.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得未必。

sentences.en: And none of the 50s prime ministers were particularly divisive.
sentences.zh: 而且50年代的首相们没有一个特别具有分裂性的。

sentences.en: I suppose what's distinctive about Mrs Thatcher is that being divisive was part of her self-image, that she kind of reveled in it, whereas most prime ministers tend not to.
sentences.zh: 我想撒切尔夫人与众不同之处在于，具有分裂性是她自我形象的一部分，她甚至以此为乐，而大多数首相往往不会这样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: If she thought if you were not being divisive, that showed you weren't, you weren't, you had no guts.
sentences.zh: 如果她认为如果你不表现出分裂性，那就说明你没有胆量。

sentences.en: You weren't in the arena.
sentences.zh: 说明你没有身处竞技场中。

sentences.zh: 保守党人经常谈论自己是“一个国家”的保守党人，对吧？

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们是这么说的。

sentences.en: And they bash Labour politicians, they say they're class warriors, they're fomenting class war and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们抨击工党政客，说他们是阶级斗争的战士，在煽动阶级战争以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So they sort of, part of the Tory message is often to say there is no division, actually, and we should all just be one happy family.
sentences.zh: 所以他们常常传达这样一种保守党信息：实际上根本没有分裂，我们本该是一个快乐的大家庭。

sentences.en: And vote Tory.
sentences.zh: 然后投票给保守党。

sentences.en: Yeah, sort of Stanley Baldwin.
sentences.zh: 对，有点像斯坦利·鲍德温。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, that's, I knew you'd have a good answer for that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我就知道你对此会有很好的回答。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's, I think that's enough of modern history.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，现代历史就聊到这里吧。

sentences.en: Can we get to a far more interesting topic?
sentences.zh: 我们能聊聊一个更有趣的话题吗？

sentences.en: Namely the Bronze Age.
sentences.zh: 也就是青铜时代。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, looking at the publicity for Stephen Fry's new book, there's one line in particular,
sentences.zh: 那么，看斯蒂芬·弗라이新书的宣传时，有一句话特别吸引人，

sentences.en: Enter the World of Troy and the Most Legendary Story Ever Told.
sentences.zh: 走进特洛伊的世界，聆听史上最传奇的故事。

sentences.en: Well, is it the most legendary story ever told?
sentences.zh: 那么，这真的是史上最传奇的故事吗？

sentences.en: I suppose it is, Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 我想是的，汤姆·赫兰德。

sentences.en: That's quite a claim, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这口气可不小，对吧？

sentences.en: But tell us, okay, so for the modernists among us, tell us in no more than about 40 words the entire story of the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 但给我们讲讲吧，对于我们这些现代主义者，请用不超过40个字讲完特洛伊战争的整个故事。

sentences.en: Okay, the world's most beautiful woman, the daughter of Zeus, Helen, is abducted by a Trojan prince called Paris to the city of Troy.
sentences.zh: 好的，世上最美丽的女人、宙斯的女儿海伦，被一个叫帕里斯的特洛伊王子拐到了特洛伊城。

sentences.en: All the Greeks have sworn an oath that if Helen gets stolen by anyone, they will go and get her back.
sentences.zh: 所有的希腊人都发过誓，如果海伦被任何人抢走，他们就会去把她夺回来。

sentences.en: So, the heroes of Greece are kind of duty-bound to sail to Troy.
sentences.zh: 所以，希腊的英雄们有责任扬帆远航去特洛伊。

sentences.en: They camp in front of the walls of Troy for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 他们在特洛伊城墙前扎营了10年。

sentences.en: Terrible and heroic deeds are done.
sentences.zh: 发生了可怕而英勇的事迹。

sentences.en: One, great heroes fight, great heroes die.
sentences.zh: 伟大的英雄们互相战斗，伟大的英雄们战死。

sentences.en: At the end, the only way that the Greeks can get into Troy is to play a trick.
sentences.zh: 最后，希腊人进入特洛伊的唯一方法就是使用计谋。

sentences.en: They build a huge wooden horse.
sentences.zh: 他们造了一匹巨大的木马。

sentences.en: They leave it, supposedly, as an offering to Poseidon, the god of the sea.
sentences.zh: 他们把它留下，据说是作为对海神波塞冬的献祭。

sentences.en: In fact, the Greeks have hidden their best warriors inside the belly of the horse.
sentences.zh: 事实上，希腊人把他们最勇猛的战士藏在了木马的腹中。

sentences.en: The Trojans rather stupidly take the horse inside Troy.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊人相当愚蠢地把木马拉进了特洛伊城。

sentences.en: The Greeks come out, they burn Troy, they all go home.
sentences.zh: 希腊人从里面钻出来，烧毁了特洛伊，然后全都回家了。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Wow, Tom.
sentences.zh: 哇，汤姆。

sentences.en: You're very good at these little summaries, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你非常擅长做这种小结。

sentences.en: If the history doesn't work out, you can always.
sentences.zh: 如果历史搞不成了，你随时可以去……

sentences.en: So, this is the question, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，问题就在这里，对吧？

sentences.en: Did it actually happen?
sentences.zh: 这真的发生过吗？

sentences.en: And give us a year, pin yourself down to a year or at least a century.
sentences.zh: 给我们一个年份，具体到一个年份或者至少一个世纪。

sentences.en: Well, the Greek historians gave various dates and they would range by our dating system for kind of 1250 to 1150 BC.
sentences.zh: 嗯，希腊历史学家给出了各种日期，按我们的年代系统来算，大约从公元前1250年到公元前1150年。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's the end of the Bronze Age.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那是青铜时代的末期。

sentences.en: And the huge question is, when the Greeks wrote about the Trojan War, and I suppose specifically
sentences.zh: 而巨大的问题在于，当希腊人书写特洛伊战争时，我想具体来说就是

sentences.en: Homer, who's the great poet, who everybody else who writes about the Trojan War stands in his shadow, were they drawing on authentic memories of something that actually happened?
sentences.zh: 荷马，那位伟大的诗人——所有其他写特洛伊战争的人都活在他的阴影之下——他们当时是在借鉴真实发生过的事情的可靠记忆吗？

sentences.en: And there have been various opinions about that over the course of time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，对此一直有各种各样的看法。

sentences.en: The Greeks and the Romans were fairly convinced that it had happened.
sentences.zh: 希腊人和罗马人相当确信这件事发生过。

sentences.en: They gave various accounts of it, various versions of it.
sentences.zh: 他们给出了关于它的各种记载、各种版本。

sentences.en: There was no kind of definitive version, although Homer was kind of as close to definitive as they got.
sentences.zh: 并没有什么绝对权威的版本，尽管荷马的版本已经算是最接近权威的了。

sentences.en: By the 18th, by the beginning of the 19th century, people were coming to assume that it was a fairy tale, that it had no roots in fact at all.
sentences.zh: 到了18世纪，到了19世纪初，人们开始认为这只是个童话，它完全没有任何事实根基。

sentences.en: And then the German businessman turned archaeologist, Heinrich Schliemann, famously decided that he was going to prove it had happened.
sentences.zh: 然后，由德国商人转行而成的考古学家海因里希·施里曼，做出了一个著名的决定，他要证明这件事确实发生过。

sentences.en: And using Homer, he went to what's now kind of the north of Turkey.
sentences.zh: 他利用《荷马史诗》，来到了现在差不多是土耳其北部的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, so where are we?
sentences.zh: 对，所以我们在哪儿？

sentences.en: Let me interrupt you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 打断你一下，汤姆。

sentences.en: Where are we exactly?
sentences.zh: 我们究竟在哪里？

sentences.en: Is this a sort of roundabout Gallipoli, am I right?
sentences.zh: 这地方是不是在加里波利附近，我没记错吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's by Gallipoli.
sentences.zh: 对，就在加里波利附近。

sentences.en: So you think of the Aegean separating Greece and what's now Turkey.
sentences.zh: 所以你想想爱琴海，它分隔了希腊和现在的土耳其。

sentences.en: You think of the narrow strip of water that separates Europe from Asia and leads into the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 你想想那条将欧洲和亚洲分隔开、通往黑海的狭窄水道。

sentences.en: Troy commands the entrance to those straits.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊扼守着这些海峡的入口。

sentences.en: So you can see that it would, you know, it's strategically significant.
sentences.zh: 所以你能看出，你知道的，它具有重要的战略意义。

sentences.en: Schliemann goes there, he digs it up, supposedly.
sentences.zh: 施里曼去了那里，据说他把它发掘了出来。

sentences.en: I mean, and when we say dig it up, I mean, he really digs it up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我们说发掘时，我是说他是真的在大力发掘。

sentences.en: He digs a massive great trench and demolishes vast swathes of the archaeology and discovers what he claims to have been Homer's Troy.
sentences.zh: 他挖了一条巨大无比的战壕，摧毁了大量考古遗迹，并发现了据称是荷马笔下的特洛伊。

sentences.en: And I guess the consensus of archaeologists now would be that this is the site.
sentences.zh: 而且我想现在考古学界的共识大概是，这里就是那个遗址。

sentences.en: It's a hill called Hisilic, that this probably was Troy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个叫希萨利克的山丘，这可能就是特洛伊。

sentences.en: And we know that this is where the Greeks and the Romans thought the battle had been fought, because in the wake of Alexander's conquest, a town grows up there,
sentences.zh: 我们知道希腊人和罗马人曾认为那场战役就是在这里打响的，因为在亚历山大征战之后，那里兴起了一座城镇，

sentences.en: which is a kind of homage to the original Troy.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上算是对最初的特洛伊的一种致敬。

sentences.en: Well, they definitely thought it happened, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们绝对坚信这事发生过，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because I've just been writing a children's book about Alexander the Great, and there's a great moment in it when they pitch up the Macedonians.
sentences.zh: 因为我刚刚写了一本关于亚历山大大帝的儿童读物，里面有一个很棒的桥段，讲述了马其顿人安营扎寨时的情景。

sentences.en: They're invading Persia, and Alexander makes a special trip to Troy to what he thinks is the tomb of Achilles.
sentences.zh: 他们当时正在入侵波斯，亚历山大特意绕道去了特洛伊，来到了他认为是阿喀琉斯之墓的地方。

sentences.en: And he does what we all do when we visit the graves of our ancestors.
sentences.zh: 然后他做了我们所有人去凭吊祖先墓地时都会做的事。

sentences.en: He takes all his clothes off, anoints himself in oil, and then runs round and round.
sentences.zh: 他脱光了衣服，在身上涂满橄榄油，然后绕着墓地一圈又一圈地奔跑。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's classic behaviour on a Turkish trip.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是去土耳其旅游时的经典行为。

sentences.en: We've all done it.
sentences.zh: 我们都这么干过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, and before that, so Alexander says that he is invading Asia to get revenge for the Persians who had invaded Greece back in 490 and 480 BC.
sentences.zh: 对，而且在此之前，亚历山大宣称他入侵亚洲是为了替公元前490年和480年入侵希腊的波斯人复仇。

sentences.en: And that had been led by Xerxes, the king of Persia.
sentences.zh: 那次入侵是由波斯国王薛西斯领导的。

sentences.en: And Xerxes, when he led his invasion, he went to the site of Troy and paid his respects to the heroes.
sentences.zh: 薛西斯在领导入侵时，曾去过特洛伊遗址，并向英雄们表达了敬意。

sentences.en: I mean, this was kind of good PR.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这算是一种很好的公关手段。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And this sense that the Trojan War is a kind of decisive moment in an ongoing war between East and West, between Asia and Europe, is very much a theme that the Greeks pick up on.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊战争是东西方、亚洲与欧洲之间持续冲突中的一个决定性时刻，这种观念非常深受希腊人认可。

sentences.en: And it's elaborated by Herodotus, who is the first great historian.
sentences.zh: 并且由第一位伟大的历史学家希罗多德进行了详细阐述。

sentences.en: Translated by me, folks, again, rush out and buy.
sentences.zh: 朋友们，这是由我翻译的，赶快去抢购吧。

sentences.en: Oh, very good plug.
sentences.zh: 哦，这个广告打得真好。

sentences.en: Yeah, just getting that, slipping that one in.
sentences.zh: 对，就是顺便提一下，巧妙地塞进去。

sentences.en: Quality plug.
sentences.zh: 高质量的广告。

sentences.en: So Herodotus rationalises the abduction of Helen as basically being something not very important.
sentences.zh: 所以希罗多德把海伦被绑架一事合理化，认为这根本算不上什么大事。

sentences.en: And his take is that the Greeks massively overreact.
sentences.zh: 他的看法是希腊人的反应过度了。

sentences.en: I mean, Herodotus basically says, we've all stolen a princess or two.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，希罗多德基本上是在说，我们谁没偷过一两个公主呢。

sentences.en: I mean, it's ridiculous to overreact.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，反应过度未免太可笑了。

sentences.en: So it's almost like a bit sort of a false flag operation or something.
sentences.zh: 所以这感觉倒有点像是一场虚假旗帜行动之类的。

sentences.en: I think Herodotus, you know, he begins his history.
sentences.zh: 我觉得希罗多德，你知道的，他是从他的历史著作开始写的。

sentences.en: So this is the first passage of prose of any work of history ever written.
sentences.zh: 所以这是有史以来任何历史著作中的第一段散文。

sentences.en: And it's about how people in Asia and people in Greece are constantly stealing each other's princesses.
sentences.zh: 内容是关于亚洲人和希腊人如何不断地互相绑架对方的公主。

sentences.en: And Herodotus is...
sentences.zh: 而希罗多德他……

sentences.en: And he really thought this happened.
sentences.zh: 他是真的认为这事发生过。

sentences.en: Yeah, he thinks it happened.
sentences.zh: 对，他认为这发生过。

sentences.en: He thinks it happened.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这真的发生过。

sentences.en: And also, interestingly, Thucydides, who is the next great historian who follows after Herodotus, who's famously sceptical, he also thinks it happens.
sentences.zh: 同样有趣的是，继希罗多德之后的下一位伟大的历史学家修昔底德，以怀疑精神闻名，他也认为这发生过。

sentences.en: But he provides the kind of rationalist perspective on it.
sentences.zh: 但他提供了一种理性主义的视角。

sentences.en: And he says that he doesn't think that it was about Helen at all.
sentences.zh: 他说他认为这根本与海伦无关。

sentences.en: He thinks that it was about wealth.
sentences.zh: 他认为这关乎财富。

sentences.en: And that Agamemnon, who is the leading king, the king of Mycenae, the richest city, and who was kind of commander in chief at Troy,
sentences.zh: 阿伽门农作为领头君王、迈锡尼（最富有的城市）的国王，同时也是特洛伊之战的某种总司令，

sentences.en: that he was so powerful that he could get all the various Greek kings together and lead a common expedition.
sentences.zh: 他权势滔天，能够把各个希腊国王召集在一起，领导一场共同的远征。

sentences.en: And Thucydides thinks that this is all about kind of controlling trade routes and stuff.
sentences.zh: 修昔底德认为这一切其实都是为了控制贸易路线之类的事情。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, he's a MarxiSt.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，他是个马克思主义者。

sentences.en: He thinks it's all about the search for profit.
sentences.zh: 他认为这一切全是为了追逐利润。

sentences.en: He's very...
sentences.zh: 他非常……

sentences.en: He's a kind of very...
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常……

sentences.en: His perspective is very much that of a strategist, someone who doesn't have much place for fantastical tales of abducted princesses.
sentences.zh: 他的视角非常符合战略家的特点，一个不给关于被绑架公主的神话故事留太多余地的人。

sentences.en: And I guess that that's probably the perspective that many modern historians would have as well,
sentences.zh: 我想这也是许多现代历史学家可能会持有的视角，

sentences.en: that this is a war that's happening in the context of great power politics and attempts to control trade routes and things like that.
sentences.zh: 即这场战争发生在宏观强权政治以及试图控制贸易路线等背景之下。

sentences.en: It's not about beautiful princesses being abducted.
sentences.zh: 而不是因为什么美丽的公主被绑架了。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So the temptation is to see it as Europe versus Asia, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以人们很容易把它看作是欧洲对阵亚洲，对吧？

sentences.en: But my sense is that that would be completely wrong, because isn't this just generally the Greek-speaking world?
sentences.zh: 但我的直觉是这完全大错特错，因为这难道不普遍就是希腊语世界吗？

sentences.en: Isn't Troy...
sentences.zh: 难道特洛伊……

sentences.en: I mean, what would Troy have been?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特洛伊究竟算什么？

sentences.en: Would it have been a Greek-speaking city, a Hittite city?
sentences.zh: 它是一座说希腊语的城市，还是一座赫梯城市？

sentences.en: So the Hittites are the people in Anatolia, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 赫梯人是安纳托利亚的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, what is it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它到底是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so the Hittites are a key part of trying to understand what the actual Trojan War might have been.
sentences.zh: 对，所以要理解真正的特洛伊战争可能是什么样的，赫梯人是其中关键的一环。

sentences.en: And the Hittites rule an empire across what's now Turkey, Anatolia.
sentences.zh: 赫梯人统治着一个横跨现今土耳其和安纳托利亚的帝国。

sentences.en: And at the beginning of the 20th century, a kind of cache of royal correspondence was found.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪初，人们发现了一批皇家信件档案。

sentences.en: And so over the course of the 20th century, these have been deciphered.
sentences.zh: 于是在整个20世纪里，这些信件都被破译了。

sentences.en: And there are a couple of letters that cast potential light on the Trojan War.
sentences.zh: 有几封信件可能为揭示特洛伊战争提供了线索。

sentences.en: So one of them mentions a town called Willusa.
sentences.zh: 其中一封提到了一个叫维鲁萨（Willusa）的小镇。

sentences.en: Sounds just like Troy.
sentences.zh: 听起来就像特洛伊。

sentences.en: Well, but another name for Troy was Ilium.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过特洛伊的另一个名字是伊利昂（Ilium）。

sentences.en: So you can see that there's potentially a kind of bleed there from Willusa, perhaps, to Ilium.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出，从维鲁萨到伊利昂之间可能存在某种名称上的演变痕迹。

sentences.en: And what's also interesting is that the king of Willusa is a man called Alexandu.
sentences.zh: 同样有趣的是，维鲁萨的国王是一个叫亚历山杜（Alexandu）的人。

sentences.en: And an alternative name for Paris, the prince who abducts Helen, is Alexander.
sentences.zh: 而拐走海伦的王子帕里斯，他的另一个名字就是亚历山大。

sentences.en: So, you know, maybe there's a mesh there.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这其中也许有什么契合之处。

sentences.en: And the other letter is a letter addressed to the king of a land called Akiwawa.
sentences.zh: 另一封信则是写给一个名为阿基瓦瓦（Akiwawa）的土地的国王的。

sentences.en: Gosh, you said that very nicely.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你念得真好听。

sentences.en: My Hittite is fluent.
sentences.zh: 我的赫梯语很流利。

sentences.en: And Akiwawa sounds, again, a bit like Achaia.
sentences.zh: 而阿基瓦瓦听起来，又有点像阿凯亚（Achaia）。

sentences.en: And Achaeans is what Homer, writing in perhaps the second half of the 8th century BC, calls the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 荷马（大约在公元前8世纪下半叶写作）将希腊人称为阿凯亚人。

sentences.en: So perhaps the Achaeans, the Achaia, which Homer is using, is a trace element of Akiwawa.
sentences.zh: 所以也许荷马所使用的阿凯亚人、阿凯亚，正是阿基瓦瓦残存的痕迹。

sentences.en: But the key thing about this is that nobody really would care about this very obscure kind of Bronze Age diplomacy, war, whatever,
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，如果不是因为荷马写下了如此惊艳的诗篇，

sentences.en: were it not for the fact that Homer had written this amazing poetry.
sentences.zh: 而且这些诗篇代代相传流淌至今，

sentences.en: And that that poetry has then kind of descended down through the century.
sentences.zh: 根本没有人会关心这种晦涩难懂的青铜时代外交、战争或其他什么东西。

sentences.en: So your son, you know, you're reading it to your son.
sentences.zh: 所以你的儿子，你知道的，你正在读给他听。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What is it about the Trojan War?
sentences.zh: 特洛伊战争的魅力究竟在哪里？

sentences.en: Presumably, I mean, he's not interested in, you know, trade routes through the Hellespont.
sentences.zh: 想必，他对赫勒斯滂海峡的贸易路线肯定不感兴趣。

sentences.en: No, he loves the Hittites.
sentences.zh: 不，他热爱赫梯人。

sentences.en: He's really into the Hittites.
sentences.zh: 他真的非常迷恋赫梯人。

sentences.en: No, you're right.
sentences.zh: 不，你说得对。

sentences.en: I think it's the, what is it?
sentences.zh: 我想这是，到底是什么呢？

sentences.en: That's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: I think, I mean, obviously with the Iliad, it's the personalities, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我认为，显然对于《伊利亚特》来说，吸引人的是个性，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's the, and it's the slightly unexpected, I mean, to a modern sensibility, it's a very unexpected story.
sentences.zh: 还有那些，以现代人的审美来看，稍微有些出乎意料、非常奇特的故事情节。

sentences.en: So Achilles, the great hero, spends half the time sulking in his tent and refusing to come out.
sentences.zh: 所以大英雄阿喀琉斯有一半时间都在帐篷里生闷气，拒绝出来。

sentences.en: There's a sort of incongruity.
sentences.zh: 这里有一种不协调感。

sentences.en: There's this odd disconnect between the sort of heroic status of the characters.
sentences.zh: 这些角色的英雄地位之间存在着一种奇特的断层。

sentences.en: And often they're quite, to modernise Weasley behaviour, which I think is intriguing.
sentences.zh: 而且通常它们相当符合现代人那种有点滑头的小心思，我觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, also, I mean, an interesting thing about it is that if you look at the Iliad, which is Homer's account of the Trojan War,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，还有一个有趣的地方，如果你看看《伊利亚特》（这是荷马对特洛伊战争的记述），

sentences.en: there's not actually very much about the Trojan War there.
sentences.zh: 里面其实并没有太多关于特洛伊战争的内容。

sentences.en: It's a very short space of time.
sentences.zh: 它所涵盖的时间跨度非常短。

sentences.en: So lots of the most famous things, say like the Trojan horse, the Trojan horse isn't in, it's not in the Iliad.
sentences.zh: 所以很多最著名的桥段，比如特洛伊木马，其实并不在《伊利亚特》里。

sentences.en: And the Trojan horse is a great story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 特洛伊木马是个很棒的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the Trojan horse is this, I mean, clearly this sort of, this, you know, this mythic sort of, this dissection of hubris,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特洛伊木马这东西，显然是一种神话般的对傲慢的解剖，

sentences.en: this moment of great craftiness, this sort of plot by the Greeks, this sort of heist, effectively, that comes off.
sentences.zh: 这是展现极高智谋的时刻，是希腊人精心策划的阴谋，实际上是一场大劫案，而且成功了。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it always seemed to me a ridiculous plot.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在我看来这总是一个荒谬的阴谋。

sentences.en: You're Trojans, you've been suffering a war for a siege for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 你们是特洛伊人，已经忍受了一场长达十年的围城战。

sentences.en: The Greeks go, and there's a huge great horse.
sentences.zh: 希腊人撤了，然后留下了一匹巨大的木马。

sentences.en: You're going to have a bit of suspicion, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 你们会有点怀疑，不是吗？

sentences.en: Are you?
sentences.zh: 会吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there's actually a wooden horse at the site of ancient Troy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在古代特洛伊的遗址上其实真的有一匹木马。

sentences.en: So the Turkish authorities have built a wooden horse and it sits there outside their site.
sentences.zh: 所以土耳其当局建造了一匹木马，就放在他们遗址的外面。

sentences.en: It doesn't look great, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，它看起来不怎么好。

sentences.en: It's not terribly impressive.
sentences.zh: 并不是特别壮观。

sentences.en: How many do you think it would fit in?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这东西能塞进去多少人？

sentences.en: Seven?
sentences.zh: 七个？

sentences.en: I don't know, ten?
sentences.zh: 我不知道，十个？

sentences.en: That would be enough, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就够了，不是吗？

sentences.en: But they just needed to open the gates, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们只需要打开城门就行了，对吧？

sentences.en: They don't need to storm the whole city.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要强攻整座城市。

sentences.en: Don't they just get in and open the gates?
sentences.zh: 他们不就是混进去然后打开城门吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that how it works?
sentences.zh: 事情不应该是这样的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they open the gates, but there are enough of them to start the slaughtering and the pillaging.
sentences.zh: 对，他们打开城门，但里面的人数足够开始大开杀戒和掠夺了。

sentences.en: I mean, you wouldn't do that with seven people, would you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不会只带七个人去干这事吧？

sentences.en: No, you need more than that.
sentences.zh: 不，你需要更多的人。

sentences.en: It's got to be quite a big horse.
sentences.zh: 它必须是一匹相当大的马。

sentences.en: Listen, let's take some questions, because questions about the Trojan War have a very, very long pedigree.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们来回答一些问题，因为关于特洛伊战争的问题有着非常非常悠久的历史渊源。

sentences.en: The Emperor Tiberius, when he was retired on Capri, used to hold the equivalent of a pub quiz.
sentences.zh: 皇帝提比略在卡普里岛退隐期间，经常举办相当于现在的酒吧问答之类的小测验。

sentences.en: About the Trojan War?
sentences.zh: 关于特洛伊战争的？

sentences.en: Yeah, and he would ask some kind of difficult questions like, so Achilles, the great hero, when he was a boy, was disguised as a girl.
sentences.zh: 对，他会问一些刁钻的问题，比如：大英雄阿喀琉斯小时候曾被伪装成女孩。

sentences.en: And Tiberius would say, what name did Achilles have as a girl?
sentences.zh: 然后提比略会问：阿喀琉斯作为女孩时的名字是什么？

sentences.en: And Odysseus, the cunning hero who comes up with the idea of the Trojan War, he has a very, very long voyage back home, and he sails past sinister creatures called the Sirens,
sentences.zh: 还有奥德修斯，那个想出特洛伊木马点子的聪明的英雄，他回家的航程非常非常漫长，他航行经过了被称为塞壬的邪恶生物，

sentences.en: who sing beautifully and then devour the Sirens, who are lured to their island.
sentences.zh: 她们歌声优美，然后会吞食那些被诱骗到她们岛上的塞壬……哦不，是水手。

sentences.en: And Tiberius wanted to know what the song was that the Sirens sung.
sentences.zh: 提比略想知道塞壬唱的是什么歌。

sentences.en: And he would expect people to know this, would they know it?
sentences.zh: 他期望人们能知道这个，他们会知道吗？

sentences.en: Well, he would.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他会的。

sentences.en: And there was one of his guests who cheated and got hold of the questions before they were asked.
sentences.zh: 当时他的一个客人作弊了，在问题提出之前就弄到了答案。

sentences.en: So what do you think Tiberius did to him?
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得提比略对他是怎么做的？

sentences.en: Threw him off the rug?
sentences.zh: 把他从地毯上扔下去？

sentences.en: Had him killed.
sentences.zh: 把他处死了。

sentences.en: Don't cheat if you go to a pub where he's run by a Caesar.
sentences.zh: 如果你去参加一个由恺撒运营的酒吧问答，千万别作弊。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's come back to the questions that we've been asked.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，让我们回到刚才向我们提出的一些问题上来。

sentences.en: But Tom, I think we should take a break firSt.
sentences.zh: 但是汤姆，我觉得我们应该先休息一下。

sentences.en: OK, well, listen, before we take the break, I'm going to read you Carl Johan's or Johan's question.
sentences.zh: 好吧，听着，在休息之前，我要把卡尔·约安（Carl Johan）或约安的问题念出来。

sentences.en: And you can have a ponder because I'm going to put you, we have to answer this.
sentences.zh: 你可以思考一下，因为我要抛给你，我们必须回答这个问题。

sentences.en: What war or event, he asks, comes closest to being of similar significance to the modern West as Troy was to the Greeks?
sentences.zh: 他问：对现代西方而言，哪场战争或事件在重要性上最接近特洛伊之于古希腊人？

sentences.en: Good question.
sentences.zh: 好问题。

sentences.en: Let's have a break.
sentences.zh: 我们休息一下。

sentences.en: Welcome back, everybody, to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎大家回到《历史的余烬》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.en: So just before the break, Tom asked me Carl Johan's question, which is, what war comes close to being of similar significance to the modern West as Troy was to the Greeks?
sentences.zh: 就在休息前，汤姆问了我卡尔·约安的问题，即：哪场战争在重要性上最接近特洛伊之于古希腊人？

sentences.en: So it seems to me, Tom, that the obvious answer to that is, I mean, the blatantly obvious answer is World War II.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，汤姆，最显而易见的答案是——明显得不能再明显的答案就是第二次世界大战。

sentences.en: I mean, World War II is the event that sort of lingers in the Western psyche as the ultimate symbol of man's humanity to man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，第二次世界大战作为人类对人类暴行的终极象征，至今仍然萦绕在西方人的精神世界中。

sentences.en: It's the ultimate morality tale.
sentences.zh: 这是一个终极的道德故事。

sentences.en: The way we structure the way we think about the world around the evil of the Nazis, the heroism of standing up to them, the dangers of appeasement, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们看待世界的方式的构建，围绕着纳粹的邪恶、挺身对抗他们的英雄主义、绥靖政策的危险，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Don't you think that the Second World War is basically our Trojan War, our mythic story?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得第二次世界大战基本上就是我们的特洛伊战争、我们的神话故事吗？

sentences.en: I think on the level of myth, but I think there's also a seasoning of the First World War, because the thing about the Trojan War is that it's pointless.
sentences.zh: 我认为在神话层面上是这样的，但我觉得其中也夹杂了一些第一次世界大战的调味，因为特洛伊战争的特点在于它是毫无意义的。

sentences.en: So if you think of the myth of the First World War is that it's, you know, what was it all for?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你回想一下关于一战的神话，那就是，你知道的，这一切到底是为了什么？

sentences.en: It was all fought in vain, people slaughtering each other in mud.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是徒劳的战斗，人们在泥泞中互相屠杀。

sentences.en: Mud flies and poppycock.
sentences.zh: 泥土飞溅，一派胡言。

sentences.en: That's pretty much what the Trojan War is.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊战争差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, it's ruinous and it's destructive and nothing really comes of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它是毁灭性的、破坏性的，而且并没有真正带来什么成果。

sentences.en: But hold on, the Greeks didn't think about it that way, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 但是等等，希腊人可不是这么想的，对吧？

sentences.en: Didn't they find it heroic and inspiring?
sentences.zh: 他们难道不觉得这很英雄气概、很鼓舞人心吗？

sentences.en: I mean, when Alexander runs around the tomb of Achilles naked, he's not thinking, you know, he's not thinking, oh, this was a complete waste of time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当亚历山大赤身裸体地绕着阿喀琉斯的坟墓奔跑时，他心里想的并不是，你知道的，他心里并没有想：哦，这完全是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the sort of Douglas Haig of the Bronze Age.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像是青铜时代的道格拉斯·黑格。

sentences.en: Well, Achilles becomes a great hero because he chooses a short life and eternal fame over a long life and obscurity.
sentences.zh: 嗯，阿喀琉斯之所以成为伟大的英雄，是因为他在长寿和平庸之间，选择了短命与永恒的声名。

sentences.en: So he's like Rupert Brooke or something.
sentences.zh: 所以他就像鲁珀特·布鲁克或什么人一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, but in the sequel, The Odyssey, we meet the ghost of Achilles in the underworld and he says it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 对，但是在续集《奥德赛》中，我们在冥界遇到了阿喀琉斯的鬼魂，他说这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: You know, I made a terrible mistake.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我犯了个大错误。

sentences.en: I'd much rather be a kind of slave working the land than be a king in the underworld.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿当个在土地上劳作的奴隶，也不愿在冥界当个国王。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think, you know, and if you look at the Greek tragedians, the Athenian tragedians and Aeschylus, one of them said that, you know,
sentences.zh: 对，而且我想，你知道的，如果你看看希腊悲剧作家、雅典悲剧作家和埃斯库罗斯，其中一个人说过，你知道的，

sentences.en: basically Greek tragedy is just kind of cuts from the great feast of Homer.
sentences.zh: 基本上古希腊悲剧只是荷马盛宴上的残羹冷炙。

sentences.en: They are incredibly bleak.
sentences.zh: 它们令人难以置信的凄凉。

sentences.en: The tragic world, the way in which terrible things happen and don't really serve a purpose,
sentences.zh: 悲剧的世界，那些可怕的事情发生却又没有真正起到什么作用的方式，

sentences.en: is absolutely a kind of riff on the idea of the Trojan War as being kind of agonisingly pointless.
sentences.zh: 绝对是对特洛伊战争那种痛苦而无意义的理念的一种即兴发挥。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, so if you fuse the First World War with the Second World War, the mix of that would give you something approximating it.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道的，如果你把第一次世界大战和第二次世界大战融合在一起，它们的混合体就会给你带来某种与之极其相似的东西。

sentences.en: Now, the producer has been pestering me with questions while you've been talking, not that he wasn't listening to you, Tom,
sentences.zh: 好了，制作人在你们谈话的时候一直在用问题纠缠我，倒不是说他没在听你讲话，汤姆，

sentences.en: but he's just been texting me with questions about Helen of Troy.
sentences.zh: 而是他一直在给我发短信，问关于特洛伊的海伦的问题。

sentences.en: Was this just a fight about a beautiful woman?
sentences.zh: 这只是一场为了一个美丽女人的争夺战吗？

sentences.en: Tell us about the woman, all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 跟我们讲讲那个女人吧，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So, yes, that's interesting, isn't it, that it's all about a woman.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这很有趣，不是吗？这一切都围绕着一个女人。

sentences.en: I mean, there aren't many real wars that are either generated by women or that have women at their sort of absolute centre, as this does.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有多少真正的战争是由女人挑起的，或者像这样把女人放在绝对的中心位置。

sentences.en: Well, I think, again, to go back to Herodotus, the history begins with an account of different people raping each other, raping each other's women.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为，再次回到希罗多德的话题，历史的开端是一段关于不同的人互相强暴、强暴彼此女人的记载。

sentences.en: And I think there is a kind of, to a disturbing degree, there is a sense that the history of war is also the history of rape.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在某种令人不安的程度上，有一种感觉：战争史同时也是强暴史。

sentences.en: So, to that extent, there is a kind of, you know, a dark truth to the story of Helen's abduction.
sentences.zh: 因此，从这个角度来说，海伦被劫持这个故事背后，确实有一种黑暗的真相。

sentences.en: But, you know, in the kind of the more romantic sense of it, we do actually have a very good question from Julian Lennox, who says,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，在某种更浪漫的意义上，我们确实有一个来自朱利安·伦克斯的非常好的问题，他说，

sentences.en: speaking of Helen, who are other historically beautiful people, specifically people whose beauty had historical significance, as in it changed the course of history.
sentences.zh: 说到海伦，还有哪些历史上美艳动人的人物，特别是那些美貌具有历史意义的人，也就是说，她们的美改变了历史的进程。

sentences.en: So, you know, do we have other women whose beauty was such that it changed the course of history?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们还有没有其他女性，其美貌足以改变历史的进程？

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I think that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是个好问题。

sentences.en: He actually said people, Tommy, didn't say women.
sentences.zh: 他其实说的是“人”，汤米，没说“女人”。

sentences.en: Yeah, he did.
sentences.zh: 对，他是这么说的。

sentences.en: I'm being sexist there.
sentences.zh: 我在这里表现出性别歧视了。

sentences.en: You've revealed your own shocking.
sentences.zh: 你暴露了你令人震惊的……

sentences.en: Yes, I'm being sexist there, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在这里表现出性别歧视了，是的。

sentences.en: That's the male gaze in action, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是“男性凝视”在起作用，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: This is a terrible moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个糟糕的时刻。

sentences.en: I think your cancellation is surely only moments away.
sentences.zh: 我想你被封杀肯定也就是几分钟的事了。

sentences.en: So, I don't know, it's an interesting one.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道，这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: Is it women or is it sexiness?
sentences.zh: 到底是女人，还是性感？

sentences.en: Because sexiness obviously does matter.
sentences.zh: 因为性感显然很重要。

sentences.en: And the example I always think of is Anne Boleyn.
sentences.zh: 我总是能想到的例子就是安妮·博林。

sentences.en: Oh, good one.
sentences.zh: 哦，这个例子好。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, the funny thing about Anne Boleyn is she's not conventionally attractive.
sentences.zh: 关于安妮·博林，有趣的是她并不是传统意义上的美女。

sentences.en: People at the time, all these sort of ambassadors at the Tudor court,
sentences.zh: 当时的人们，都德宫廷里的所有这些大使们，

sentences.en: would write back and they would say, oh, she's sallow-faced, she's sort of vulpine, you know, she's not attractive.
sentences.zh: 会在信里写道，哦，她面色发青，有点像狐狸一样，你知道的，她并不迷人。

sentences.en: She had 11 fingers, didn't she?
sentences.zh: 她有十一根手指，对吧？

sentences.en: But she, well, there's this claim about the finger as well.
sentences.zh: 不过她，嗯，关于那根手指也有这种说法。

sentences.en: I think we should probably, yeah, gloss over that.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大概应该，对，一笔带过。

sentences.en: Was that the key?
sentences.zh: 那是关键所在吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe it was.
sentences.zh: 对，也许是的。

sentences.en: Maybe she was able to put this extra finger to very potent use, who knows?
sentences.zh: 也许她能把这多出来的一根手指发挥出奇效，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Don't it.
sentences.zh: 别这样。

sentences.en: So, Anne Boleyn has this hold over Henry VIII, clearly, and he's obsessed with her.
sentences.zh: 所以，安妮·博林显然对亨利八世有着这种掌控力，他对她着迷不已。

sentences.en: And, you know, had it not been for that, but the fact that she was, you know, interested in the kind of new evangelical ideas,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，要不是因为这一点，而是因为她，你知道的，对那种新的福音派思想感兴趣，

sentences.en: the new kind of ideas critical of Catholic Church, it is perfectly plausible that England, you know,
sentences.zh: 对那种批评天主教教会的新思想感兴趣，完全合乎情理的是，英国，你知道的，

sentences.en: there would have been a Protestant movement, but the king would have fought it off, and that England would have remained a Catholic country, as France did.
sentences.zh: 本可能会有一个新教运动，但国王会把它镇压下去，而且英国本会像法国一样保持一个天主教国家。

sentences.en: So you could, you can say, with somebody like Anne Boleyn, one individual, one individual's sexual allure does hold the key to a massive structural cultural change.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以，你可以说，对于安妮·博林这样的人，某一个个人，某一个个人的性吸引力的确掌握着巨大结构性文化变革的关键。

sentences.en: So she's the face that launched a thousand monasteries being dissolved.
sentences.zh: 所以她就是那张“引发了一千座修道院被解散”的脸。

sentences.en: A thousand Bibles.
sentences.zh: 一千本圣经。

sentences.en: A thousand Bibles.
sentences.zh: 一千本圣经。

sentences.en: And what about Cleopatra?
sentences.zh: 那克利奥帕特拉呢？

sentences.en: Cleopatra's not very...
sentences.zh: 克利奥帕特拉并不是很……

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, Cleopatra is, of course, is always presumed to have been incredibly beautiful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，克利奥帕特拉，当然，人们总是想当然地认为她美得不可方物。

sentences.en: But not beautiful, right?
sentences.zh: 但其实并不美，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, if you look at her coins, she doesn't look particularly beautiful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你看她的硬币，她看起来并没有多美。

sentences.en: And I think that sex wasn't necessarily what she was offering the men she slept with, because basically we only know that she slept with two men, Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，性感不一定就是她提供给那些和她睡觉的男人的东西，因为基本上我们只知道她和两个男人睡过觉，尤利乌斯·凯撒和马克·安东尼。

sentences.en: And both of those men happen to be the most powerful men in the Mediterranean at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且这两个男人恰好是当时地中海地区最有权势的男人。

sentences.en: So I think we can...
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们可以……

sentences.en: And even when Antony dies, Cleopatra then makes a pitch at Octavian, the future Augustus.
sentences.zh: 甚至在安东尼死后，克利奥帕特拉接着又去向屋大维（即未来的奥古斯都）抛媚眼。

sentences.en: So if Melania Trump moves on to Joe Biden, we'll know that she wasn't interested in Donald for his looks.
sentences.zh: 所以如果梅拉尼娅·特朗普转而投向乔·拜登，我们就会知道她看中唐纳德可不是因为他的长相。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that that would be a reasonable presumption.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个合理的推测。

sentences.en: But, of course, in the way that Cleopatra is portrayed as a kind of fatal seductress, there is something there of Helen, the idea that the love of a beautiful woman
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，在克利奥帕特拉被塑造成某种致命尤物的过程中，里面确实有海伦的影子，也就是那种认为一个美丽女人的爱

sentences.en: can be destructive for heroes and indeed for cities.
sentences.zh: 会给英雄甚至城市带来毁灭的观念。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's absolutely part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这绝对是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Now, do we have...
sentences.zh: 那么，我们有没有……

sentences.en: We have lots more questions, don't we?
sentences.zh: 我们还有很多很多问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Give me another question.
sentences.zh: 再给我一个问题。

sentences.en: What about Josh Harold Wilson?
sentences.zh: 乔什·哈罗德·威尔逊怎么样？

sentences.en: I wonder if there's any relation to what Josh Harold Wilson says.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这跟乔什·哈罗德·威尔逊说的话有没有什么联系。

sentences.en: Is film a useful tool for exploring history or does it do more damage than good?
sentences.zh: 电影是探索历史的有用工具，还是弊大于利？

sentences.en: Well, that's very topical with The Crown, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这跟《王冠》很应景，不是吗？

sentences.en: So the film of Troy, you've seen the film of Troy, the Brad Pitt film?
sentences.zh: 所以特洛伊这部电影，你看过特洛伊这部电影吗，布拉德·皮特演的那部？

sentences.en: It's the worst film about the ancient world ever made.
sentences.zh: 那是拍过的关于古代世界的最烂的电影。

sentences.en: That's a big claim.
sentences.zh: 这口气可不小。

sentences.en: Worse than Cleopatra?
sentences.zh: 比《克利奥帕特拉》还烂？

sentences.en: Cleopatra's great.
sentences.zh: 《克利奥帕特拉》挺棒的。

sentences.en: It's very long, though.
sentences.zh: 不过太长了。

sentences.en: Very boring, as I remember.
sentences.zh: 据我记忆，非常无聊。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: Troy is the worst film ever made because it gets rid of the gods and therefore it gets rid of everything that makes Homer interesting
sentences.zh: 《特洛伊》是有史以来最烂的电影，因为它抛弃了神明，因此它抛弃了让荷马变得有趣的一切元素，

sentences.en: because without the gods, it becomes quite dull.
sentences.zh: 因为没有了神明，它就变得相当乏味。

sentences.en: And more than that, what they're trying to do with Troy is to make it historically grounded.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们试图对《特洛伊》进行的处理是让它植根于历史。

sentences.en: And the whole point is that whatever you may think about the kind of the tiny acorn of fact that gives rise to the great oak of the Trojan myth, it didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 而关键在于，无论你对那颗孕育了特洛伊神话这棵参天大树的微小事实橡子作何感想，那都是没有发生过的。

sentences.en: It didn't happen as Homer portrays it.
sentences.zh: 它并不是像荷马所描绘的那样发生的。

sentences.en: There was no Achilles.
sentences.zh: 没有阿喀琉斯。

sentences.en: There was no Helen.
sentences.zh: 没有海伦。

sentences.en: There was no Trojan horse.
sentences.zh: 没有特洛伊木马。

sentences.en: So it's all myths.
sentences.zh: 所以这全都是神话。

sentences.en: So the very attempt to try and portray it as it did is a spectacular waste of energy and effort.
sentences.zh: 因此，试图将其描绘成真实发生过的这种尝试本身，就是对精力和心血的一种极其荒谬的浪费。

sentences.en: But it's truly terrible.
sentences.zh: 但它真的是烂透了。

sentences.en: But does it do any harm?
sentences.zh: 但它有什么害处吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得。

sentences.en: I don't think it does any damage.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它有什么破坏性。

sentences.en: Probably.
sentences.zh: 大概吧。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose you can argue that films as propaganda do harm, don't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想你可以辩称，作为宣传工具的电影是有害的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they enter into the collective imagination of people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们进入了人们的集体想象之中。

sentences.en: And if what they are promoting is, you know, difference, hatred, all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果它们在宣扬的，你知道的，是分歧、仇恨、诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Well, an interesting counterpoint would be 300, which is also a film about ancient Greece and tells the story of the Spartans at Thermopylae.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一个有趣的对立面将是《300勇士》，这也是一部关于古希腊的电影，讲述了斯巴达人在温泉关的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is a brilliant portrayal of the ancient world because it very accurately portrays the Spartans as proto-Nazis, as proto-fascists,
sentences.zh: 我认为，那是对古代世界的一次极其精彩的描绘，因为它非常准确地将斯巴达人描绘成雏形纳粹、雏形法西斯，

sentences.en: which is basically what they were.
sentences.zh: 而这基本上就是他们当年的样子。

sentences.en: The Spartans were a huge inspiration to the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人给纳粹提供了巨大的灵感。

sentences.en: And one of the things that's unsettling about 300 is that it doesn't serve up the kind of morality that we expect.
sentences.zh: 而《300勇士》令人不安的一点在于，它并没有迎合我们所期望的那种道德观念。

sentences.en: The strong are strong, the weak are weak, and the weak are contemptible for being weak.
sentences.zh: 强者就是强者，弱者就是弱者，而弱者因为软弱而令人鄙视。

sentences.en: And it's very unsettling, but I think also very, very accurate.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人不安，但我认为也非常、非常准确。

sentences.en: But there's a reason, you know, 300 has become very popular with the kind of more right-wing fringes for that reason.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么，你知道的，《300勇士》正因如此在一些更偏右翼的边缘群体中变得非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: So it could be argued that that's done damage.
sentences.zh: 所以可以说这造成了危害。

sentences.en: That is interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Let's talk a bit about, since we've got onto 300 and all this stuff, about how we see the
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈，既然我们已经聊到了《300勇士》以及诸如此类的话题，谈谈我们是如何看待

sentences.en: Trojan War, how modern societies have seen the Trojans.
sentences.zh: 特洛伊战争的，现代社会是如何看待特洛伊人的。

sentences.en: So something that's always fascinated me is the fact that Geoffrey of Monmouth and sort of medieval British, sort of English and Welsh writers were fascinated by this idea that
sentences.zh: 所以有一件事一直让我着迷，那就是蒙茅斯的杰弗里以及中世纪英国、英国和威尔士的作家们着迷于这样一个观点，即

sentences.en: we are descended from the Trojans.
sentences.zh: 我们是特洛伊人的后裔。

sentences.en: There was a fellow called Brutus who was a, he was related to Aeneas, who supposedly founded
sentences.zh: 有一个叫布鲁图斯的家伙，他是埃涅阿斯的亲戚，据说埃涅阿斯创立了

sentences.en: Rome, and that Brutus basically sails across the sea with a load of Trojan refugees and founds
sentences.zh: 罗马，而布鲁图斯基本上带着一船特洛伊难民漂洋过海，创立了

sentences.en: Britannia, which is named after him.
sentences.zh: 不列颠尼亚，这个名字就是以他命名的。

sentences.en: And he separates his kingdom into three parts, England, Scotland, and Wales, which he gives to his three sons.
sentences.zh: 他把他的王国分成三部分：英格兰、苏格兰和威尔士，分别送给他的三个儿子。

sentences.en: And he founds a city called New Troy, which becomes London and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他建立了一座名为“新特洛伊”的城市，后来变成了伦敦，诸如此类。

sentences.en: What's all that about?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And the question that puzzles me is why would you empathise with the Trojans who are losers rather than the Greeks who are the winners?
sentences.zh: 让我感到困惑的问题是，你为什么会去同情身为失败者的特洛伊人，而不是身为胜利者的希腊人？

sentences.en: Because the Trojans are ultimately the winners.
sentences.zh: 因为特洛伊人最终才是赢家。

sentences.en: Because Aeneas, who you mentioned, who is the son of Aphrodite, cousin of the princes of
sentences.zh: 因为你刚才提到的埃涅阿斯，他是阿芙罗狄蒂的儿子、特洛伊诸王子的

sentences.en: Troy, he escapes Troy.
sentences.zh: 表亲，他逃出了特洛伊。

sentences.en: Supposedly, he comes to Italy and his descendants found Rome.
sentences.zh: 据说，他来到了意大利，他的后代建立了罗马。

sentences.en: So the Romans identify themselves with the Trojans.
sentences.zh: 所以罗马人将自己等同于特洛伊人。

sentences.en: So if you identify yourself with the Trojans, you're also identifying yourself with the Romans.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你把自己等同于特洛伊人，你其实也就是在把自己等同于罗马人。

sentences.en: So why did the Romans do it though?
sentences.zh: 那么，罗马人当时为什么要这样做呢？

sentences.en: Why did the Romans, is it because the Greeks were their rivals and they needed a sort of alternative origin story?
sentences.zh: 为什么是罗马人？难道是因为希腊人曾是他们的死敌，所以他们需要某种替代的起源故事？

sentences.en: They couldn't just take a Greek origin story.
sentences.zh: 他们总不能直接采用希腊的起源故事吧。

sentences.en: Because the Trojan War and Homer, you know, Homer is the prestige poet and you want a bit of it.
sentences.zh: 因为特洛伊战争和荷马，你知道的，荷马是声名显赫的大诗人，而你也想沾点光。

sentences.en: And if you can identify yourself with that story, then you're kind of joining in with it.
sentences.zh: 如果你能把自己和那个故事联系起来，那就相当于你也参与进去了。

sentences.en: And also it provides a rationale for the Romans to go and conquer Greece.
sentences.zh: 而且这也为罗马人出兵征服希腊提供了一个合理的借口。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because they can say that they're taking vengeance for the Trojans.
sentences.zh: 因为他们可以说自己是在为特洛伊人复仇。

sentences.en: And that's something that Mehmet II, the Ottoman who captures Constantinople, he makes great play with this as well.
sentences.zh: 攻占君士坦丁堡的奥斯曼苏丹穆罕默德二世也是这么大做文章的。

sentences.en: He's saying that he is ruling as the heir of the Trojans.
sentences.zh: 他自称是以特洛伊人继承人的身份在统治。

sentences.en: That by capturing Constantinople, he's taking vengeance for the sack of Troy.
sentences.zh: 通过攻占君士坦丁堡，他是在为特洛伊城的沦陷复仇。

sentences.en: And do any modern Turks think this?
sentences.zh: 现代土耳其人会这么想吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我觉得不会。

sentences.en: No, Erdogan, he's the heir of Achilles, or sorry, the heir of Hector.
sentences.zh: 不，埃尔多安，他是阿喀琉斯的继承人，哦抱歉，是赫克托耳的继承人。

sentences.en: Mehmet II, his mother was Greek.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德二世的母亲是希腊人。

sentences.en: So he was kind of plugged into that culture.
sentences.zh: 所以他算是对那种文化耳濡目染。

sentences.en: He was aware of it.
sentences.zh: 他是了解的。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, it's much more of a European thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然，这更多是一种欧洲现象。

sentences.en: But in the wake of the collapse of the Roman Empire in early medieval Europe, it's a way for people as they start to get a sense of their own identity, they look around.
sentences.zh: 但在中世纪初欧洲罗马帝国崩溃之后，当人们开始产生自我认同感时，他们便开始环顾四周寻找依据。

sentences.en: And by plugging yourself into Greek mythology, Roman history, you're giving yourself a kind of real sense of prestige.
sentences.zh: 通过将自己融入希腊神话和罗马历史，你为自己赋予了一种真正的声望感。

sentences.en: And to say that you're descended from the Trojans, I mean, that kind of multiplies it.
sentences.zh: 自称是特洛伊人的后裔，我的意思是，这简直是成倍地提升了逼格。

sentences.en: And the great thing about Britannia and Brutus coming to Britain is that Britain was supposedly a land of giants.
sentences.zh: 而关于不列颠尼亚和布鲁图斯来到不列颠，最妙的一点在于传说中不列颠曾是一片巨人的土地。

sentences.en: And I saw in the paper...
sentences.zh: 我在报纸上看到……

sentences.en: Still is.
sentences.zh: 现在还是。

sentences.en: I saw in the paper today that Boris Johnson was saying that he's now committed to having a cabinet of giants.
sentences.zh: 我今天在报纸上看到鲍里斯·约翰逊说他现在致力于组建一个由“巨人”组成的内阁。

sentences.en: So Brutus supposedly fights two giants called Gorg and Maygorg.
sentences.zh: 所以传说布鲁图斯与两个名叫戈尔格（Gorg）和马伊戈尔格（Maygorg）的巨人战斗过。

sentences.en: And it would be great to see them in the cabinet.
sentences.zh: 能看到他们在内阁里一定很棒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: In place of Gavin Williamson or somebody.
sentences.zh: 代替加文·威廉姆森（Gavin Williamson）或者什么人。

sentences.en: You don't think he's a Trojan figure?
sentences.zh: 你不觉得他是个特洛伊式的人物吗？

sentences.en: I think Gorg as Secretary of State for Education would be a lot more fun.
sentences.zh: 我觉得让戈尔格当教育大臣会带劲得多。

sentences.en: But it's a funny thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这挺有意思的，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's how this question about who you empathise with.
sentences.zh: 这就是关于你会对谁产生共情的问题。

sentences.en: So when I was reading it to my son the other night, I said, who do you want to win?
sentences.zh: 所以前几天晚上我给我儿子读这个故事时，我问他，你希望谁赢？

sentences.en: He knows the Trojans lose because kind of everybody seems to just know that they lose.
sentences.zh: 他知道特洛伊人会输，因为好像所有人打小就知道他们会输。

sentences.en: And he said, oh, well, I really like the Trojans.
sentences.zh: 而他说，哦，嗯，我真的很喜欢特洛伊人。

sentences.en: I like Hector.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢赫克托耳。

sentences.en: I know it doesn't end well for him.
sentences.zh: 我知道他最后没有好下场。

sentences.en: And I said, that's funny because I liked Hector when I was, you know, eight.
sentences.zh: 我说，真有意思，我八岁的时候也喜欢赫克托耳。

sentences.en: And I wonder whether we think differently than our predecessors might have done because we are programmed.
sentences.zh: 我在想，我们的想法是否跟先辈们有所不同，因为我们被灌输了某种观念。

sentences.en: This is, you know, this is a gift to you with your Christianity.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是基督教留给你们的馈赠。

sentences.en: Whether we are programmed to cheer for the underdog.
sentences.zh: 我们是否被潜移默化地教育去支持弱者？

sentences.en: We know the Trojans lose.
sentences.zh: 我们知道特洛伊人会输。

sentences.en: So we kind of, you know, we think they're the good guys.
sentences.zh: 所以我们自然而然地，你知道的，觉得他们是好人。

sentences.en: And the Greeks who behave so badly, squabbling about slave girls and crying and behaving in this sort of ludicrous, sort of whingy, snowflakey way.
sentences.zh: 而希腊人表现得如此糟糕，为抢夺女奴争吵不休，哭哭啼啼，行为荒谬，像个娇气包、小雪花一样。

sentences.en: Who empathises with them now?
sentences.zh: 现在谁会对他们产生共情？

sentences.en: Well, Achilles is the great hero.
sentences.zh: 好吧，阿喀琉斯是大英雄。

sentences.en: He is, you could say, hungry like the wolf.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，他就像一头对杀戮饥渴的恶狼。

sentences.en: Very good talk, Thomas.
sentences.zh: 讲得真好，托马斯。

sentences.en: So we pledge that we get a new romantic lyric in every week.
sentences.zh: 所以我们保证每周都有一次新的浪漫主义抒情。

sentences.en: And the back of the net there, I like it.
sentences.zh: 直奔球门死角，漂亮，我喜欢。

sentences.en: Oh, did it tell us?
sentences.zh: 哦，它告诉我们了吗？

sentences.en: Did it tell you?
sentences.zh: 它告诉你了吗？

sentences.en: Well, I got that one.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我猜中了那个。

sentences.en: So Achilles is the great hero.
sentences.zh: 所以阿喀琉斯是大英雄。

sentences.en: And he's a great hero because he's basically the best at killing people.
sentences.zh: 他之所以是个大英雄，是因为他基本上杀人最在行。

sentences.en: And that does seem frightening to us, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，这确实让我们感到害怕。

sentences.en: I mean, Achilles is a frightening figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，阿喀琉斯是个可怕的人物。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你说的对。

sentences.en: You mentioned Alexander.
sentences.zh: 你提到了亚历山大。

sentences.en: Alexander completely models himself on Achilles.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大完全是以阿喀琉斯为模板来塑造自己的。

sentences.en: And Alexander kills a lot of people as well.
sentences.zh: 而且亚历山大也杀了不少人。

sentences.en: And I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: I think it is essentially.
sentences.zh: 我觉得本质上就是这样。

sentences.en: He's got a view to a kill, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他一心只想杀戮，汤姆。

sentences.en: He's got a view to a kill.
sentences.zh: 他一心只想杀戮。

sentences.en: I think that our sensibilities are incredibly Christian now.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在的敏感度已经深深打上了基督教的烙印。

sentences.en: And so we are kind of programmed to identify with those who suffer, those who are the victims, those who become the slaves rather than those who do the slaving.
sentences.zh: 因此我们某种程度上被洗脑去认同那些受苦的人、受害者、沦为奴隶的人，而不是那些奴役他人的人。

sentences.en: But the initial consumers of the Iliad, the people who listen to the poets tell and retell these stories, they presumably wouldn't have thought that.
sentences.zh: 但《伊利亚特》最初的受众，那些听诗人们一遍又一遍讲述这些故事的人，他们大概不会这么想。

sentences.en: They'd have just thought these people are losers.
sentences.zh: 他们只会觉得这些人就是失败者。

sentences.en: Therefore, you know, they got what was coming to them.
sentences.zh: 所以嘛，你知道的，他们这是罪有应得。

sentences.en: Some did, but some didn't.
sentences.zh: 有些人是，但有些人不是。

sentences.en: So again, this is a massive theme in Greek tragedy, is the suffering of the losers.
sentences.zh: 所以同样地，希腊悲剧的一个核心主题就是失败者的痛苦。

sentences.en: And in a way, they're kind of, you know, one of the bleakest works of literature ever written
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它们可以说是，你知道的，有史以来最黯淡的文学作品之一

sentences.en: is Euripides' Trojan Women, which he's writing against the backdrop of the Peloponnesian War,
sentences.zh: 那就是欧里庇得斯的《特洛伊妇女》，他是在伯罗奔尼撒战争的背景下创作的，

sentences.en: the great war between Athens and Sparta, which will actually end with the defeat of Athens.
sentences.zh: 那是雅典和斯巴达之间的大战，最终以雅典的战败告终。

sentences.en: But the Athenians are sacking a lot of cities, as the Trojans do.
sentences.zh: 但雅典人在四处洗劫城市，就像特洛伊人做的那样。

sentences.en: And Euripides gives this portrayal of the queens and the princesses of Troy being rounded up after the sack of the city, about to be led off into slavery.
sentences.zh: 欧里庇得斯刻画了特洛伊王后和公主们在城市被洗劫后被押走、即将沦为奴隶的悲惨境况。

sentences.en: And it's a devastating portrait of what it means to be a victim in a war.
sentences.zh: 这是一幅极其震撼的画卷，展现了在战争中沦为受害者的真正含义。

sentences.en: And the power of it is precisely that there is no real kind of redemptive quality to it.
sentences.zh: 其力量恰恰在于其中没有任何真正的救赎质感。

sentences.en: The key thing that you get from Christianity is the idea that there is a redemptive quality in suffering.
sentences.zh: 你从基督教中得到的核心理念是，苦难中存在一种救赎的品质。

sentences.en: So if you counterpoint the sack of Troy in Greek myth to the sack of Jerusalem in the Old Testament,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你将希腊神话中的洗劫特洛伊与《旧约》中的洗劫耶路撒冷进行对比，

sentences.en: it's terrible, it's devastating.
sentences.zh: 这很可怕，极具毁灭性。

sentences.en: But the conviction that the Jews hold to is that ultimately it's expressive of God's power.
sentences.zh: 但犹太人坚信的是，归根结底这表达了上帝的力量。

sentences.en: And so therefore it is, you know, there is a purpose to it.
sentences.zh: 因此，你知道的，这是有其深刻目的的。

sentences.en: What you get in Euripides is absolutely bled of any sense of that.
sentences.zh: 而在欧里庇得斯的作品中，这种救赎感被彻底抽干了。

sentences.en: This is just, you know, terrible stuff happens.
sentences.zh: 这只是，你知道的，可怕的事情发生了。

sentences.en: And so it was that kind of Euripidean take was resurrected an awful lot during the Gulf War and the aftermath.
sentences.zh: 所以在海湾战争及其善后期间，这种欧里庇得斯式的视角在很大程度上被复活了。

sentences.en: So it was almost impossible to go to a theatre and not see a Greek tragedy in which the Greeks were the, you know, the coalition forces.
sentences.zh: 当时几乎不可能不去剧院看上一部希腊悲剧，剧中的希腊人扮演的正是，你知道的，联军部队。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 好吧，按照惯例，我们的播客以汤姆关于基督教的10分钟演讲收尾，讲讲它是如何改变现代世界的，以及为什么每个人都应该去买他的书，

sentences.zh: 我确信你们已经买过了。
